A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the current data is not sensitive enough to probe the extreme tail of non-Gaussianity and hence, the current constraints are not sensitive to the choice of prescriptions.
the current constraints on non-Gaussianity are robust, but the future constraints could be sensitive to the choice of mass function prescription.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the statistical analysis of number counts of high-redshift clusters is likely to remain an important probe of the primordial non-Gaussianty for the foreseeable future.
the extreme tail of halo mass function can be probed in a controlled way, and it is important to do so to obtain accurate constraints on the primordial non-Gaussainity.
